newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronics rise on Wall Street surge.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronics rise on Wall Street surge.

text.p: Taiwan's electronic shares rose at mid-session on Tuesday as the overnight surge by high-tech shares on Wall Street reaffirmed investors' confidence about the trend-setting sector's profit outlook, brokers said.
With 55 minutes left at 0305 GMT, electronics were up 0.73 percent while the overall index slumped 48.17 points or 0.59 percent at 8,075.09 amid investor caution.
Overall turnover was a modest T$48 billion.
Widespread gains by technology shares, including an all-time high for International Business Machine, pushed the Dow Jones industrial average to a record finish on Tuesday.
"The rise on Wall Street gave investors even more confidence about the outlook of the global high-tech industry, especially integrated circuits," said George Hou, analyst for Jardine Fleming.
Hou said sentiment also was spurred by the upcoming July 12 ex-rights date for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, the island's largest chipmaker.
Taiwan Semiconductor gained T$3.50 or 3.15 to T$114.50.
